title: WebSocket ingest backpressure & reconnect playbook
author: Aisha Rodriguez
body:
Summary

This playbook describes recommended designs, operational controls, and a runbook for WebSocket-based ingestion integrations with Redwood Inference. It is intended for partner integrators, SDK teams, and Customer Success engineers onboarding customers that prefer persistent connection models (WebSocket, bidirectional HTTP/2, or similar). The guidance focuses on: graceful backpressure handling, reconnect and resume semantics, observable signals, and actionable escalation steps when connections degrade.

When to use this playbook

- Customers sending stream-oriented events with low per-message latency requirements (telemetry, conversational tokens, streaming embeddings ingestion).
- Integrations where long-lived client connections reduce overhead and improve responsiveness compared to polling or webhooks.
- Scenarios that must tolerate transient network issues and resume without duplicate processing.

Goals and success criteria

- Maintain end-to-end ingestion availability >= 99.9% (SLO) for customer traffic under normal network conditions.
- Avoid unbounded memory growth in brokers/ingest frontends when downstream is congested.
- Provide deterministic client behavior on reconnect: at-most-once delivery where required, or exactly-once semantics where customers implement idempotency keys.

Architecture patterns (recommended)

1) Terminate WebSocket at a lightweight edge proxy
- Edge (Layer 7) terminates TLS and authenticates the initial request. Use a proxy (Envoy/NGINX) that can do connection-level limits and graceful drain.

2) Forward to an ingestion front-end with internal queuing
- The front-end should accept frames and append to a bounded in-memory queue per-tenant. When limits are reached it applies backpressure by signaling clients (close frame or application-level flow-control message).

3) Decouple consuming workers from the front-end
- Worker pool processes queued messages and writes to durable storage or message bus (Kafka/Rabbit/Cloud Pub/Sub) with independent scaling.

Client best practices

- Authenticate once with a short-lived token and include a tenant id in the opening handshake.
- Support a small receive buffer and cooperative flow control: stop sending if the server sends a "PAUSE" control frame, resume on "RESUME".
- Implement exponential backoff with jitter for reconnect attempts and cap to a reasonable ceiling (e.g., 30s).
- Preserve in-flight message IDs and provide idempotency keys for operations that must be exactly-once.
- Segment large payloads into smaller frames and apply client-side rate limiting.

Server / Redwood-internal best practices

- Per-connection quotas: configure per-tenant and per-connection message and byte rate limits. Default: 200 messages/min and 2 MB/min per connection (tunable).
- Bounded queues: use per-tenant ring buffers with a configurable max (default 10k messages). When full, apply backpressure rather than unbounded allocation.
- Control frames: implement a minimal control protocol on top of WebSocket (CONTROL {type: "PAUSE" | "RESUME" | "ACK" | "NACK"}) to signal clients.

Reconnect and resume semantics

- Lightweight resume: clients include a resume_token assigned by the front-end in the opening handshake. The front-end keeps a short-lived in-memory window mapping tokens -> last-ack position (recommended TTL: 90s).
- Durable resume (for higher guarantees): instruct clients to checkpoint offsets into a durable store (e.g., tenant-state API) after receiving server ACKs.

Backpressure strategies (ordered preference)

1) Cooperative flow-control (preferred)
- Server sends "PAUSE" -> client throttles send rate. Server sends periodic "RESUME" to allow more data.

2) Token bucket token exchange
- Server grants credits to client; client can send up to credits. When depleted, client must stop until new credits arrive.

3) Explicit close with retry hint
- If a tenant exceeds absolute safety limits, close connection with a close code and a retry-after in the close payload. Example: Close(4001, "retry-after=15").

4) Drop oldest (safest for memory control)
- As a last resort, drop oldest messages in the per-tenant ring buffer and emit a metric and audit event. Documenting dropped events is required for customers.

Observable signals and metrics (recommended Prometheus names)

- websocket_connections_total{tenant} (gauge)
- websocket_active_connections{tenant,region} (gauge)
- websocket_messages_in{tenant} (counter)
- websocket_messages_dropped{tenant,reason} (counter)
- websocket_flowcontrol_paused{tenant} (gauge 0/1)
- websocket_resume_requests{tenant} (counter)
- websocket_resume_successes{tenant} (counter)
- websocket_reconnects{tenant} (counter)
- websocket_resume_latency_seconds{quantile="0.5|0.95|0.99"} (histogram)

Alerting thresholds (examples)

- P1: websocket_messages_dropped > 100/min for any enterprise tenant -> page SRE oncall.
- P2: websocket_reconnects increase 10x above baseline in 10m -> create incident and notify CSM.
- P3: websocket_flowcontrol_paused == 1 for > 2m for any top-10 tenant -> create Slack alert to #cs-ops and #platform-ops.

Operational runbook: triage steps

1) Initial intake (first 10 minutes)
- Validate tenant and region in the alert. Pull the last 15 minutes of websocket logs and metrics.
- Check if front-end CPU/memory is saturated, and inspect per-tenant queue occupancy and drop counters.

2) Customer-facing actions (10–30 minutes)
- Communicate immediately via the agreed channel (customer Slack or support ticket): "We have observed increased reconnects/drops. Our team is investigating. Please hold client restarts until we advise."
- If the client is aggressively reconnecting, ask the customer to temporarily increase reconnect jitter or disable immediate retry for 30–60 seconds.

3) Mitigation (30–90 minutes)
- Apply throttles or rate-limits at the edge for the tenant to prevent system-wide destabilization.
- If queue is full and safe, scale worker pool or increase retention for the tenant temporarily (follow capacity guardrails).

4) Root cause & follow-up (90m–7d)
- Correlate with downstream latency, storage write errors, or third-party queue instabilities.
- Produce an RCA for incidents meeting major-incident criteria; include impact, timeline, mitigations, and permanent fixes.

Escalation matrix (owners and contacts)

- First responder: Customer Success Engineer (owner_team: customer-success) -> Slack: @cse-oncall -> Pager: CSE rota.
- Platform on-call: Platform SRE -> Slack: #platform-oncall -> Pager duty: platform-sre.
- Product/ML OPS: for model or runtime regressions affecting throughput -> @mlops-lead.
- Exec escalation: Customer Success Manager -> escalates to Sales/Revenue Ops for high-impact SLAs.

Testing and validation checklist (pre-onboarding)

- Synthetic congestion test: run a client that increases message rate to 3x expected peak and verify backpressure triggers within 90s.
- Resume test: disconnect after N messages, reconnect using resume_token and validate no duplicates or gaps as per configured semantics.
- Chaos test: simulate transient backend errors (DB timeouts, message-bus spikes) and assert system remains within SLO with degradation modes well signaled.

Rollout checklist (for customers moving from webhooks to WebSocket ingestion)

1) Planning
- Confirm tenant capacity profile with Redwood CSM and ensure quotas are provisioned.
- Agree on monitoring workspace and alert routing.

2) Canary (single-tenant)
- Onboard a single production tenant into a canary pool. Run for 72 hours with synthetic traffic.

3) Scale (10% incremental)
- Increase the number of canary tenants in 10% increments while monitoring message_dropped and reconnects.

4) Production cutover
- Schedule a 2-hour maintenance window. Notify customer and Redwood stakeholders. Roll traffic gradually and observe for 2 maintenance windows before full cutover.

Appendix A: example handshake and control frames

- Opening handshake (client -> server):
{
  "type": "OPEN",
  "tenant_id": "tenant-1234",
  "auth_token": "redacted",
  "resume_token": "optional-client-token"
}

- Server PAUSE frame payload: 
{
  "type": "CONTROL",
  "control": "PAUSE",
  "reason": "upstream-backpressure",
  "retry_hint_seconds": 10
}

- Server close example (explicit):
Close code: 4001
Close payload: "retry-after=15;reason=tenant-rate-limit-exceeded"

Appendix B: sample Prometheus alert rule (YAML snippet)

- rule: HighWebsocketDrops
  expr: increase(websocket_messages_dropped[5m]) > 100
  for: 2m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "High websocket message drops for {{ $labels.tenant }}"
    description: "Investigate per-tenant queue pressure and worker throughput."
